title: Include residency audit events in export allowlist + add Splunk/Sentinel samples
author: Kevin Osei
description: Motivation: Hosted data residency enforcement introduces new audit event types (residency.policy_evaluated and residency.violation). During beta we discovered these events were being dropped by the exporter default filters (only a subset of security/compliance event types were allowlisted), which breaks SIEM evidence collection and confuses customers who were expecting to see violations in Splunk/Sentinel (ref SUP-4077). This PR updates the exporter filter configuration to include residency audit events, adds minimal field-mapping tests to prevent regressions, and documents sample payloads + recommended Splunk/Sentinel parsing queries. Scope: exporter allowlist + docs only (no schema changes to the core audit event payload). Rollout: safe to deploy independently; new events will start flowing automatically once the audit-log-exporter is updated. Validation: unit tests updated and manual replay of fixture payloads through the exporter with Splunk HEC + Sentinel DCR sample configs.
commits: exporter: add residency.* event types to default allowlist
tests: add fixtures for residency.policy_evaluated + residency.violation and assert routing/serialization
docs: add Splunk HEC sample, Sentinel DCR mapping, and example queries
chore: clarify config comments + bump docs linter settings
implementation_notes: Allowlist: add exact matches for event_type values 'residency.policy_evaluated' and 'residency.violation' (no wildcarding to avoid accidentally exporting future experimental residency event types without review).

Export format: no changes; residency events are forwarded as-is in the JSON body with standard envelope fields (event_id, occurred_at, actor, org_id, project_id, request_id, region, decision, reason_code).
Docs: include a compact sample payload (policy_evaluated allow + violation deny), plus Splunk props/transforms guidance and Sentinel KQL examples for filtering by org_id and region.
Back-compat: existing customers with custom allowlists must explicitly add these event types if they fully override defaults (documented in README note).
review_conversation: Marcus Lin: Please confirm we’re not broadening export surface area beyond these two event types (I don’t want a wildcard residency.* allow). Also, do the docs mention that custom allowlists override defaults?

Kevin Osei (author): Confirmed: exact event_type matches only; no wildcard. Added README note + docs callout: if you override allowlist, you must include residency.policy_evaluated and residency.violation explicitly.

Olga Petrov: For evidence, we need fields org_id, project_id, region.effective, decision, reason_code, and request_id to be visible in the exported record. Can we add a regression test that asserts those keys exist in the fixture and survive serialization?
Kevin Osei (author): Added fixture key assertions in allowlist test and a serialization snapshot test for Splunk HEC payload wrapper to ensure the envelope doesn’t drop nested keys.
Logan Wright: Any concern about volume? policy_evaluated could be high frequency. We should document recommended filters for customers (e.g., export violations only, or sample policy_evaluated).

Kevin Osei (author): Good point. Added guidance in both Splunk/Sentinel docs: export both for full evidence, but if volume is a concern, customers can filter to decision=deny or reason_code!=OK and keep policy_evaluated for a sampled subset.
Nadia Rahman: Can you include the region fields naming explicitly (requested/evaluated/effective) so customers don’t confuse endpoint region with execution region?
Kevin Osei (author): Updated docs and sample payloads to show requested/evaluated/effective and added a short definitions section.
final_review_state: Approved by Marcus Lin, Olga Petrov, Logan Wright
release_notes: Audit-log-exporter now exports residency.policy_evaluated and residency.violation audit events by default; includes Splunk/Sentinel documentation and sample payloads for SIEM onboarding.
